name: @wippy-session/wippy-form
title: Session Form
description: Renders a session ask_user form (single/multiple choice with Other) and submits the answer back to the owning session.

wippy.description: Renders one Session `ask_user` form as a question card and sends the answer back to the owning session through the Host's artifact-state API. Each question supports per-answer notes and, when the definition allows it, an Other free-text row. A form with several questions shows one at a time, with a counter and a review step before sending. Once the answer is accepted, the card becomes a read-only summary. The inputs are `definition` (the questions and options), `form-version` (a version other than 1 disables submission), and `state` (`active` while the form can be answered, `idle` after it was answered). The component loads and submits by itself, so the tag only needs these attributes. Agents must never write the `<wippy-form>` tag, because it is created only through the Session `ask_user` tool.

form-version.description: Form definition schema version (currently 1). A value other than 1, from this prop or from the loaded state's own `form_version`, disables the interactive form and shows the notice "This form needs a newer version of the app." instead.

definition.description: The questions to ask: `title`, optional `description`, and `fields`, a list of choice questions, each `{ id, type: "choice", label, description?, required, options: [{value, label, description?}], multiple, allow_other }`. Optional `submit_label` and `answered_message` are accepted and not shown. A definition with no fields shows an error message.

state.description: Package-tag lifecycle state mirrored from the artifact: "active" (still answerable) or "idle" (already answered, shown read-only). Changing this prop triggers a reload of the canonical form state from the Host.

density.description: Question-card sizing: "compact" (default) or "comfortable", a larger size/spacing scale. Read purely through the `:host([density="comfortable"])` CSS selector — no JS reads it — but must be a declared prop so the package-tag mount path can set it as an attribute.
